hpi_details: 50M reporting shoe and ring size increase over 3 years along with frontal headaches and joint aches. Elevated IGF-1 and non-suppressible GH on OGTT.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acromegaly is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes pituitary MRI with gadolinium and referral for transsphenoidal resection, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: enlarging hands and feet with coarsening facial features
Key HPI features: 50M reporting shoe and ring size increase over 3 years along with frontal headaches and joint aches. Elevated IGF-1 and non-suppressible GH on OGTT.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 74, BP 142/88. Prominent supraorbital ridges, spade-like hands, prognathism, mild joint tenderness. Bloods: Serum IGF-1 elevated for age; 75g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) fails to suppress Growth Hormone.
Relevant background/PMH: No significant chronic medical history
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acromegaly.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Simple weight gain/aging without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Visual field changes.
management_principles: Refer to neurosurgery for transsphenoidal tumor resection; consider medical therapy (somatostatin analogs or Pegvisomant) if residual tumor post-op
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 74, BP 142/88. Prominent supraorbital ridges, spade-like hands, prognathism, mild joint tenderness. Bloods: Serum IGF-1 elevated for age; 75g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) fails to suppress Growth Hormone.
reference_soap.assessment: Acromegaly secondary to GH-secreting pituitary adenoma.
reference_soap.plan: Pituitary MRI with gadolinium. Refer to neurosurgery for transsphenoidal tumor resection; consider medical therapy (somatostatin analogs or Pegvisomant) if residual tumor post-op.

learning_objectives: Recognize subtle chronic somatic changes characteristic of acromegaly
Interpret IGF-1 screening and OGTT growth hormone suppression confirmation tests

teaching.one_liner: Excess growth hormone from a pituitary adenoma causing gradual enlargement of the hands, feet, and facial features, confirmed by elevated IGF-1.
